newsitem.title: UK: Rank gains ahead of year-end results.
newsitem.headline: Rank gains ahead of year-end results.

text.p: Shares in Rank Group Plc rose on Monday, rebounding from recent weakness ahead of the leisure group's annual results on Thursday, dealers said.
The stock, which has underperformed the rest of the UK market by more than 20 percent over the past year, was up 11-1/2p at 423 by 1418 GMT. Volume was an unexciting 1.3 million shares.
"The stock is just having a run up ahead of the figures," said one market-maker. "Every dog has its day."
Analysts were reluctant to say today's bounce could signal an end to the stock's underperformance.
"It has underperformed by over 20 percent over the past year and there has been no shortage of publicity about what the company is trying to do," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.

"But the issue is not the fundamentals of the company, it is market sentiment." He said there was no reason yet to think sentiment was improving towards the stock, which dropped in December, after a disappointing trading statement.

"Ultimately the company has some pretty good market positions and if (chief executive Andrew) Teare can kick it into action it could improve its performance," said Matthew Naylor, analyst at Williams de Broe.
"But I don't think the market is ready to focus on that yet."

In its statement in December, Rank said turnover at its Hard Rock restaurants, regarded as a key unit for the company, fell four percent on a same store basis in the 11 months to the end of November, though Teare said the company was making good trading and strategic progress in a year of transition.
